blocks.name: bit-membership
blocks.note: Numeric-uint32 and signed-bit-pattern forms are both explicit; bit-pattern forms avoid unnecessary unsigned scalar coercion.

blocks.name: fixed-width-word-composition
blocks.note: Generic, caller-range-proven, and initialization-prepared cross-word shift profiles coexist. Configured/fixed shift distances can precompute 32-count or count-32 once, deleting one SUB from every hot shift.

blocks.name: first-next-set-bit
blocks.note: Set-bit/cardinality profiles reuse caller-owned lane facts. A known high lane uses firstSetHighBitIndex32 without lane selection; cardinalityClass32 applies whenever exactly one lane remains relevant, including two-lane callers that already proved the other lane empty.

blocks.name: popcount
blocks.note: Exact popcount profiles now cover fixed fused SWAR, set-bit sparsity, high-lane emptiness, high<=10 table lookup, and their combined distribution/cache profile. Selection remains explicit from configured width, occupancy distribution, and cache evidence.

blocks.name: coordinate-decode
blocks.note: Coordinate decode has table-backed generic profiles and initialization-selected power-of-two geometry profiles. Power-of-two columns use mask/shift and can omit coordinate tables when no other consumer needs them.

blocks.name: legal-landing-cell
blocks.note: Initialization may index landing cells by physical column or move slot. If a caller already observed the current landing cell for scoring, legality, or a known-cell transition, playableKnownCell32 reuses that scalar and avoids a second load. Otherwise playableColumn32 remains the direct load+compare form.

blocks.name: winning-line-test
blocks.note: Winning-line containment supports signed/unsigned one- and two-lane forms. Initialization should partition immutable required masks into low-only, high-only, and cross-lane groups; single-lane groups use maskContainsI32/maskContains32 directly, leaving two-lane functions only for masks that actually span lanes.

blocks.name: apply-undo-state-transition
blocks.note: Transition profiles include center-slot specialization for odd-width center-omitted layouts. When the caller already knows it is executing the omitted center slot, zero support arithmetic disappears; low-lane moves that remain low also avoid any meta load/store.

blocks.name: hash-mix32
blocks.note: Three explicitly costed hash-mix strengths let the application trade bucket avalanche against cycles.

blocks.name: transposition-cache-probe
blocks.note: TT probe retains the prepared index. Full replacement writes tag+value for misses/replacements; proven hits may use ttUpdateValue32 to update only the value and avoid an identical tag store.

blocks.name: canonical-reflection-symmetry
blocks.note: Reflection supports register-only configured networks, byte-contribution tables, and exact C3/C4 cache profiles. Exact tables are admitted only where 2 KiB/16 KiB storage can plausibly remain L1-hot and beat the 6/9-cycle register networks; cache and allocation costs stay explicit.

blocks.name: frontier-antichain-normalization
blocks.note: Frontier normalization now has signed/unsigned, one-/two-lane, and seeded lazy-compaction profiles. Signed bit-pattern storage is cheapest when selectable; Uint32 owners retain bit-31 correctness while still avoiding the first candidate and accepted-prefix rewrites.

blocks.name: residual-transition
blocks.note: Residual transitions support both class-major and action-major prepared-base layouts. Class-major fits fixed-class/varying-action loops; action-major fits the pinned fixed-action/varying-class residual loop. Initialization transpose cost remains explicit.

blocks.name: move-order-selection
blocks.note: Candidate selection supports generic count, exact array-backed configured counts 2..10, and scalar-producer configured counts 2..10. Scalar profiles apply only when score production already owns values as live scalars; initialization selects arity once with no hot width dispatch.

blocks.name: alpha-beta-bound-update
blocks.note: Alpha-beta primitives include ordinary bound updates/cutoff plus cutoff-first child-result predicates. When the caller already has alpha<beta, testing value>=beta or value<=alpha first removes bound-update work on cutoff paths without increasing non-cutoff serial cost.

blocks.name: shared-atomic-claim-release
blocks.note: Atomic release has notifying and no-notify profiles. Polling or externally awakened consumers select atomicReleaseNoNotify32 and pay only the publication store; Atomics.wait users retain atomicRelease32 so wake semantics are not weakened.

blocks.name: shared-queue-enqueue-dequeue
blocks.note: Queue sequence comparisons are performed in the Int32 domain. Equality-first nonblocking profiles retain their fast-path reduction, while dequeue-ready values are explicitly normalized across 0x7fffffff -> -2147483648 rollover. Owned/shared and blocking/nonblocking profiles otherwise remain unchanged.

blocks.name: capacity-growth-rehash
blocks.note: Capacity growth keeps allocation and rehash costs explicit. rehashOverwrite32 now performs only migration; new capacity is caller-known from newMask and is not reconstructed/returned by the primitive.
